counterfactual_missing_items: No ipsilateral autonomic features such as lacrimation, conjunctival injection, or nasal congestion are supplied
No attacks of 15-180 minutes are described; the headaches last 3-7 days
No continuous pain background, indomethacin response, or acute-medication overuse frequency is supplied
decisive_items: A 36-year-old woman with a 17-year history of migraine headaches

She typically had 3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days, with relief only from sumatriptan after trials of acetaminophen, ibuprofen, rizatriptan, methylprednisolone, prednisone, and dexamethasone failed
Brain magnetic resonance imaging was unremarkable
response.rationale: R1 is anchored to the longitudinal migraine history and high-frequency, prolonged attacks, with unremarkable MRI supporting a primary headache; R3 shares an orbital/facial radiation span but lacks the autonomic features required for a trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia and remains a category-level guess. Other candidates either duplicate R1, name a treatment response, or depend on features absent from the raw spans.

rejected.why: Treatment failure is not a diagnosis; the sphenopalatine ganglion block response does not identify a headache disorder.
Cluster headache requires short 15-180 minute attacks and ipsilateral autonomic features, neither of which is supplied.
No raw support spans; continuous pain and indomethacin response are not in the vignette.
The pain is described as long-lasting headache, not paroxysmal/electric/triggered trigeminal neuralgia, and radiation extends beyond the trigeminal branches.
The listed medications were failed trials, not evidence of overuse; no frequency/duration of acute medication use is supplied.
Redundant append-only restatement of R1 with the same raw span and no independent evidence.
